notes:
Round 55, printer row. 8 printer records plus 1 substrate record (Mauritania - does NOT count on the printer row).

FILED:
- ZWE: searched "Fidelity Printers and Refiners Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe prints banknotes ZiG"; fetched Fidelity Gold Refinery's own history page (fgr.co.zw/?p=287), which states FPR's business at inception in 1966 was largely to print secure banknotes in the basement of the old Reserve Bank building, and that in 2021 the printing division was spun off as the Printing and Minting Company of Zimbabwe. Filed to FPR. The named-next-step mirror mriguide.com/zimbabwe-the-reserve-bank-of-zimbabwe-has-begun-the-production-of-redesigned-zig-banknotes/ was fetched and names NO printer (only "better substrate"). The Fidelity DENIAL story (nehandaradio.com/?p=44771) was not needed.
- MDV: searched "Maldives Monetary Authority rufiyaa polymer banknotes printed by De La Rue"; De La Rue's own launch release, reproduced in full on coinweek.com, says the 2015 six-note family "was printed on Safeguard by De La Rue". (marketscreener mirror of the same release returned Access Denied.)
- BMU: searched "Bermuda Monetary Authority new banknote series printed by De La Rue launch"; BMA press release PDF of 30 Oct 2024 says the new $2 and $5 "banknotes printed by De La Rue on SAFEGUARD polymer substrate".
- KHM: banknotenews query; newest Cambodia entry (200,000 riel, 16.10.2024) gives Printer: (Banknote Printing Works of the National Bank of Cambodia). Central bank's own works. weak_source true.
- URY: named next step. banknotenews Uruguay entries; B558a (2,000 peso, intro 27.04.2016) gives Printer: OBERTHUR fiduciare. weak_source true.
- TKM: banknotenews newest Turkmenistan entry (200 manat commemorative, intro 01.12.2025) gives Printer: (De La Rue), polymer Safeguard. weak_source true.
- YEM: searched Yemen/Goznak; Moscow Times (18 Jun 2020) quotes Russian MFA spokeswoman Zakharova saying Goznak has been printing money for Yemen's government under a 2017 commercial contract, after 64bn riyals of Russian-printed notes were seized in Aden. Strong news source.
- BDI: banknotenews newest circulating Burundi entry; B243a 2,000 franc dated 11-09-2023 gives Printer: (Oberthur Fiduciaire). The newer 2025 Burundi item (10,000-franc Mietens numismatic product, ?p=46050) gives Printer: (Unknown). weak_source true.
- ERI: searched "Bank of Eritrea nakfa banknotes printed by Giesecke Devrient"; only Wikipedia states it ("printed by German currency printer Giesecke & Devrient"). Filed weak_source true; no bank document found.

SUBSTRATE ONLY (flagged, not printer-row):
- MRT: banknotenews 50-ouguiya 2023 commemorative lists Printer: (Unknown) but names three substrates - Landqart Durasafe, Oberthur paper-with-sisal, Louisenthal Hybrid. Filed one Landqart substrate record; Mauritania stays absent on the printer row.
- ZMB: re-confirmed as substrate-only. Fetched the named next step https://www.diplo.news/en/articles/erfolgreiche-lancierung-der-neuen-kwacha-banknotenserie-in-sambia - it is a Landqart release saying only that the Kwacha 10 and 20 "have been printed on Landqart AG's innovative Durasafe substrate" and that the Bank of Zambia thanked Landqart. No printer named. Also fetched https://currency-news.com/news/2025/may/02/new-currency-family-celebrates-the-natural-beauty-of-zambia/ - paywalled after the first two paragraphs (no printer in the free part). Zambia remains absent on the printer row.

RULED OUT THIS ROUND (read, nothing filable):
- UGA: searched Bank of Uganda printing contract; fetched https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/government-gives-printing-deal-to-german-firm-1709514 - the July 2017 award went to Veridos Identity Solutions GmbH (beating De La Rue International and Muhlbauer/Hungarian Banknote Printing), but the article stresses that the minister's letter "does not mention the word 'currency' anywhere" and that Bank of Uganda was not copied. Not a banknote-printing statement. Hand-check candidates not fetched: https://independent.co.ug/bou-complained-to-money-printer-for-breach-of-contract and https://www.centralbanking.com/node/1604174.
- ISR: fetched https://boi.org.il/en/economic-roles/banknotes-and-coins/third-series-of-the-new-shekel-2014/ (via WebFetch; curl is blocked by Radware) - names the designer Osnat Eshel and issue dates but NO printer. Hand check: https://boi.org.il/en/communication-and-publications/press-releases/information-on-the-new-series-of-banknotes/ (curl blocked, not WebFetched).
- IRQ: Arabic search for a CBI printing tender; fetched the Al Jazeera piece https://www.aljazeera.net/ebusiness/2025/2/1/... which says only that Iraq reprinted its currency after 2003 with "the world's largest companies, including British and German firms" - no firm named.
- AZE: banknotenews newest entry (100 manat, intro 15.07.2026, ?p=49844) gives Printer: (Unknown).
- GIN: banknotenews newest entry (20,000 franc sig/date 2024, ?p=46511) is a variety note with no Printer field at all.
- MDG: banknotenews ?p=41359 names l'Imprimerie Officielle de Tananarive, but for 1917 colonial 20-franc notes that were NEVER ISSUED - not a record for the current central bank. No modern ariary printer found.
- GEO: named next step. Fetched https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banking/news/2444659/innovative-print-techniques-are-key-for-new-georgian-banknotes - paywalled, only headline and standfirst visible. Also fetched https://nbg.gov.ge/en/media/news/on-the-issuance-of-5-and-20-lari-banknotes-of-2021-emission-in-circulation (curl returns navigation chrome only, body not in the HTML) and https://securamonde.com/news-2/banknotes/georgia-circulates-5-lari-banknote/ (security features only, no printer). Georgian-language search hit the matsne.gov.ge decree "Rule on the production of lari banknotes and coins" (https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/1019210) which returned Access Denied to curl - HAND CHECK THAT URL, it is the most likely place to find a Georgian state printing works named.
- MDA: searched Romanian for a BNM printing tender; results were bulk mtender.gov.md attachment blobs. Fetched https://bnm.md/files/BDF_moldavie_50lei_1.pdf (slow, ~4.3 MB) - it is a public security-features leaflet, no printer named.
- BIH: searched Bosnian for a CBBH banknote-printing tender and for Oberthur; fetched https://www.ohr.int/convertible-marka-currency/ (1998 OHR release approving the KM design - no printer). No printer statement found.
- CUB: Spanish search; fetched https://oncubanews.com/cuba/economia/pesos-cubanos-tendran-billetes-mas-seguros (2014 BCC security-feature announcement, no printer).
- HTI: banknotenews ?p=33456 (2021 report of 2,500- and 5,000-gourde notes) names no printer.
- DJI: banknotenews query returned no Djibouti note entry with a Printer field; nothing fetched beyond search.
- NOT ISSUERS, no printer row possible: MNE (uses the euro unilaterally, issues no banknotes), SMR (euro; coins only, struck in Italy), PSE (no national currency), ECU, SLV, TLS (fully dollarized - the circulating notes are US dollars from the US Bureau of Engraving and Printing, which is not these central banks' printer; filing BEP to them would misstate the relation, so they are left absent).

Veins: the local-press tender vein produced nothing this round for BIH, MDA, IRQ or AZE - the searches returned procurement-portal blobs and aggregator noise rather than reported contracts. The issuing-bank press release vein worked once (Bermuda). BanknoteNews was the workhorse: 9 country queries, 4 usable Printer fields (KHM, URY, TKM, BDI), 5 with (Unknown) or no field. 'Ask whether the bank runs its own works' produced Cambodia and, historically, Zimbabwe.

records.detail: Fidelity's own corporate history states that at inception in 1966 Fidelity Printers and Refiners' business was largely to print secure banknotes, done in secrecy in the basement of the old Reserve Bank building at 79 Samora Machel Avenue in Harare, moving to purpose-built premises at No. 1 George Drive, Msasa in 1978-82; in 2021 the printing division was split off into a new company, the Printing and Minting Company of Zimbabwe.

De La Rue's launch release states that the new Maldives family of six banknotes - Rufiyaa 10, 20, 50, 100, 500 and 1000 - launched on 1 November 2015 was designed by local designer Abdullah Nashaath and was printed on Safeguard by De La Rue in close association with the Maldives Monetary Authority.
records.source_title: Maldives Launches New Family of Polymer Banknotes (De La Rue press release)

records.detail: The Bermuda Monetary Authority's press release of 30 October 2024 announces that the new $2 and $5 banknotes printed by De La Rue on SAFEGUARD polymer substrate will enter circulation that autumn, Bermuda's first polymer notes and among the first to carry King Charles III's effigy; De La Rue's currency managing director Ruth Euling says it was a privilege to design and deliver them.
records.source_title: Bermuda Monetary Authority Releases New $2 and $5 Banknotes Printed on Polymer

records.entity: Banknote Printing Works of the National Bank of Cambodia
records.detail: BanknoteNews records the printer of Cambodia's 200,000-riel commemorative note (B438a), issued 16 October 2024 for the 20th anniversary of King Norodom Sihamoni's coronation, as the Banknote Printing Works of the National Bank of Cambodia; the note is 170 x 76 mm on paper with a 10-mm holographic stripe and a demetalized NBC security thread.
records.source_title: Cambodia new 200,000-riel commemorative note (B438a) confirmed introduced 16.10.2024

records.detail: BanknoteNews records the printer of Uruguay's revised 2,000-peso series B note (B558a), dated 2015 and introduced by the Banco Central del Uruguay on 27 April 2016 with a holographic windowed security thread and SPARK map of Uruguay, as Oberthur Fiduciaire.

BanknoteNews records the printer of Turkmenistan's commemorative 200-manat note (B243a), introduced 1 December 2025 for the 30th anniversary of permanent neutrality, as De La Rue; the note is 150 x 75 mm on Safeguard polymer with a holographic stripe showing the Arkadag monument in PureImage.

Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova confirmed that Goznak has been printing money for Yemen's government under a commercial contract signed in 2017, after separatists in Aden seized a convoy carrying 64 billion riyals (about US$255 million) of Russian-printed banknotes that Russia had printed for Yemen's central bank in June 2020.
records.source_title: Yemen Separatists Seize $225M in Russian-Printed Cash - The Moscow Times

records.detail: BanknoteNews records the printer of Burundi's 2,000-franc note (B243a), dated 11 September 2023 and signed Musharitse/Murengerantwari, as Oberthur Fiduciaire; the 132 x 66 mm paper note carries a green-to-gold OVI pineapple with embossed BRB and a windowed thread demetalized with a heifer's head and BRB.

Wikipedia's article on the Eritrean nakfa states that the current series of banknotes is the artwork of banknote designer Clarence Holbert and is printed by the German currency printer Giesecke & Devrient; no Bank of Eritrea document confirming this was found, so the record rests on an encyclopaedia entry alone.

BanknoteNews reports that the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie's 50-ouguiya note commemorating 50 years of the ouguiya, unveiled 15 June 2023 and introduced 18 June 2023, was issued on three substrates - Durasafe composite by Landqart, paper with sisal by Oberthur, and Hybrid by Louisenthal - while the printer itself is listed as unknown.
records.source_title: Mauritania new 50-ouguiya commemorative note (B131a-c) confirmed introduced on 18.06.2023
